This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/ Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned counsel for the State.
Perused the application as well as documents annexed thereto.

3. The present application has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. thereby invoking the inherent power of this Court to quash the entire criminal proceeding in G.R. No.22 of 2017 arising out of F.I.R. No.25.11.2017 of the Golanthara P.S., Berhampur vide P.S. Case No.182 of 2017 for commission of alleged offences under Sections 341, 323, 294, 506, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 34 I.P.C. read with Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act, and Section 3 of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and the same is now pending before the learned 2nd Additional & Sessions Judge,
Berhampur.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner at the outset contended that although the petitioner was initially not named in the F.I.R., however on the basis of the co-accused statement he has been implicated in the present case.

He further submitted that in the meantime the case has been split up in respect of the some of the co-accused persons and in such split up case the trial has already taken place and that the accused persons have been acquitted.

In such view of the matter, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that since the co-accused persons have been acquitted there is a no possibility of the petitioner being convicted in such trial and as such the criminal case against the Srikanta Sahu vs State Of Odisha .....

1 petitioner be quashed.
5. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand objected to the quashing of the criminal proceeding on the grounds taken in the application.
He further contended that in the event some of the co- accused persons have been acquitted the petitioner can take the advantage of such acquittal during this trial in the split up the case.

6. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsels appearing for the parties, on a careful examination of the background facts, further keeping in view the fact that the split up trial has been concluded in respect of other co-accused persons, the present application is being disposed of by directing the trial court to make every endeavor to expedite the trial and conclude the same preferably within a period of six months from the date of communication of a certified copy of today's order.
The petitioner is directed to co-operate in the conclusion of the present trial.
7. With the aforesaid observations and directions, the CRLMC stands disposed of.
( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra)
